scope: Critical literal-G7 repair for exactly eight China-countable P4 survivors. Proposal only: no ledger, state, P4, selection, routing, or longlist file is modified.

binding_interpretation.G7: A bounded 2026-2029 de-risking path, a named 2030-2034 trigger or an official 2028-2035 customer-system trigger, readiness/window analysis, and at least two independent timing records, including one primary or official record. Host-system timing counts only where the proposed product performs a necessary or tightly coupled job.
binding_interpretation.china_beachhead: The existing China flag may remain countable when a named lawful customer or channel and exact-category route exist; a future startup feature need not already have its own purchase order. Product-scope, origin, restricted-party screening, and end-use conditions remain binding.
binding_interpretation.score_method: Only a source-supported raw-score restoration is proposed. One raw point in launch_window_fit_2030 adds 1.6 weighted points; one raw point in competition_whitespace adds 1.8 weighted points. No other criterion is changed.

summary.quality_note: All eight pass the literal timing-source test after repair, but each remains marginal because the evidence is a necessary host-system/category trigger rather than a purchase order for the future startup product. C-13 is the weakest timing repair; F-12's G4 repair remains marginal.

best_replacements_if_main_adjudicator_re.reason: Best existing China-capable non-L14 replacement: official CEPC build-to-about-2035 timing plus an exact 96-system klystron/PSM bill and industrial-collaboration path.
Second-best existing China-capable non-L14 replacement: JCET production-equipment factory phase completes in H2 2028 and two exact plasma-cleaner tenders establish the category route.

timing_sources.claim: Xinhua's official-government-hosted report states that BEST aims in 2030 to achieve net fusion power gain and demonstrate power generation using a compact high-field route.
timing_sources.locator: HTML title/date and paragraphs containing '2030', 'net power gain', 'demonstrate power generation', and 'compact high-field'.

timing_sources.claim: Energy Singularity's primary roadmap specifies a compact high-field HTS tokamak at equivalent Q greater than 2 in 2030 and a commercial-potential fusion demonstration plant in 2035.

ideas.category_linkage: REBCO tape acceptance metrology is tightly linked: S01 says BEST needs more than 1,500 km of HTS tape, one CS coil consumes hundreds of kilometers, and Shanghai Superconductor completed batch supply and full-scale magnet qualification. Long-reel acceptance cannot be inferred from generic fusion spend; it is an explicit material-production job.
ideas.bounded_2026_2029_path: 2026-2027 benchmark against THEVA Tapestar on Shanghai Superconductor-class REBCO reels; 2028 complete local-origin instrumentation and high-field correlation; 2029 require one paid production-line evaluation with pre-agreed Ic-map and defect-escape criteria.
ideas.window_and_risk: BEST and Energy Singularity provide two independent 2030/2035 HTS-host triggers. The window is real but crowded: THEVA already sells the exact Tapestar class, and Shanghai Superconductor has internal process knowledge. Kill the China leg if no paid line evaluation exists by end-2029.
ideas.china_route: A locally manufactured, independently developed acceptance scanner sold to Shanghai Superconductor-class civilian HTS producers. Screen every end use and exclude controlled magnet-design know-how from the product.

score_impact.reason: Two independent primary/official 2030-2035 HTS-fusion roadmaps plus exact quantified REBCO consumption repair the timing record.

unresolved_non_G7_risks: THEVA Tapestar is a direct incumbent.
No paid startup-line evaluation yet.
G4 and G6 remain marginal.

timing_sources.claim: Dongguan's official 2020-2035 industrial plan explicitly prioritizes high-power industrial fiber, semiconductor, and ultrafast lasers; upstream laser components including pump-source packaging; standardization and industrialization, all under its 2035 horizon.
timing_sources.locator: PDF pages 31-34 for the 2035 target and page 43, lines/paragraph beginning 'actively deploy high-end laser equipment manufacturing', especially pump-source packaging and industrialization.

timing_sources.claim: The 2026 China fiber-laser market record shows current manufacturer volume and margin dynamics, providing a present design-in base independent of the 2035 government roadmap.
timing_sources.locator: Evidence pack demand section describing Raycus Q1 2026 revenue and profitability; use only as market timing, not as a permitted buyer.

ideas.category_linkage: The plan names semiconductor lasers and pump-source packaging, so a precision current/power driver is a necessary operating subsystem rather than a generic laser adjacency. Outsourcing of that driver is not proven and remains the commercial kill test.
ideas.bounded_2026_2029_path: Remove Raycus from the buyer list immediately. By 2027 freeze a clean, independently developed China product line; in 2028 place a driver evaluation with one officially screened civilian industrial-laser OEM such as Han's Laser only after counsel clearance; by 2029 require a paid design-in and thermal/lifetime benchmark.
ideas.window_and_risk: The official plan closes the literal 2035 roadmap gap, but it is aspirational and does not name a driver procurement. Incumbent vertical integration and sanctions screening make this the weakest G7 repair.
ideas.china_route: Domestic-origin driver hardware and firmware, civilian industrial-laser end uses only, no transfer of US directed-energy design data. Raycus is excluded because it is Entity Listed; Han's Laser or any substitute requires fresh official-list and ownership screening before contact.

score_impact.reason: An official 2035 high-power-laser and pump-component roadmap now exists, but the absence of a named driver procurement caps the restored score at 3.

unresolved_non_G7_risks: Raycus is prohibited as a base-case buyer.
Driver outsourcing is not evidenced.
Clean-room US/CN product partition and buyer screening remain G6 conditions.

timing_sources.claim: CNNC states that its 50 MW molten-salt-storage plus supercritical-CO2 generation demonstration, launched in 2024 and selected in the fifth national first-set equipment batch, is expected to complete demonstration application in 2028.

ideas.category_linkage: A printed-circuit heat exchanger/recuperator is a thermodynamically necessary heat-recovery element in a closed sCO2 Brayton power block; the 50 MW 2028 project is therefore a tightly linked host-system trigger. Final acceptance still requires the project's actual heat-exchanger architecture to be confirmed.
ideas.bounded_2026_2029_path: 2026 map duty cycle and channel geometry against Chaotan One; 2027 demonstrate diffusion-bonded coupon integrity and fouling tolerance; 2028 qualify a full-scale recuperator module with a civilian EPC or component supplier; 2029 require a paid design-in for the 50 MW follow-on or a steel-plant retrofit.
ideas.window_and_risk: The 2028 first-set demonstration creates a credible 2030-2034 scale-out window, but CNNC says it has complete turnkey supply capability. VPE and domestic integrators can absorb the component.
ideas.china_route: Local industrial manufacture and civilian waste-heat/thermal-storage use. No reliance on nuclear-reactor procurement or controlled nuclear design information.

score_impact.reason: The CNNC primary record supplies the missing official 2028 project trigger, while the operating reference plant supplies independent readiness timing.

unresolved_non_G7_risks: CNNC claims complete turnkey capability.
Exact PCHE bill of materials for the 50 MW project is not public.
VPE remains a strong direct incumbent.

ideas.non_cosmetic_wedge: The incumbent products are vertically integrated or supplier-specific. The proposal does not compete at cell monitoring, pack BMS, fire suppression, or propulsion control. It independently proves selectivity and insulation-monitor coordination at the replaceable pack-to-vessel-bus boundary and cryptographically binds the installed pack identity/configuration to the approved protection dossier. That changes the safety case for mixed-brand replacement and retrofit fleets; a UI-only layer would not.
ideas.bounded_2026_2029_path: 2026 freeze a class-facing fault/selectivity and configuration schema with one shipyard and surveyor; 2027 bench-test two brands of pack/BMS against one vessel DC bus; 2028 install on a subsidized retrofit; 2029 require two paid standalone RFQs or one paid fleet framework. Kill if buyers accept only a bundled battery-vendor product.
ideas.window_and_risk: The 2028 subsidy cliff pulls retrofit procurement forward and the 2030 safety/technical regime sustains qualification work. Fast absorption by Racern, CATL/CALB, Dukosi/Yichuan, Chuangwei, or Danfoss remains likely.
ideas.china_route: Civilian inland and service vessels, local manufacture/integration, CCS-facing evidence, restricted-party screening, and no structurally restricted shipyard as the base-case buyer.

changes.reason: The narrowed cross-vendor protection/configuration boundary is non-cosmetic and distinct from five named integrated substitutes, but it is not yet purchased.
Official subsidy through 2028 and a separate official 2030 safety/technical regime create two independent in-window triggers.

unresolved_non_G7_risks: No paid standalone gateway RFQ.
Incumbents can add cross-vendor adapters.
The original broad interoperability product remains a G4 fail; only the narrowed boundary product passes marginally.
